messages:
tara: Quick sync 9:05am PT 026-02-12 1 0 - ran A/B for v3-quant-lite vs v2.9-fp16 on canary traffic. win on latency/cost but a wobble on code-qa slice.
alex: saw latency drop ~18% p50 and cost/token ~22% down. Nice. what's the wobble?
tara: code-qa (short code completions) MRR delta = -0.018, p=0.031, n=4800. exact_match delta = -0.006, p=0.12. eval-bot attached the run.
eval-bot: A/B summary: slice=code-qa(short); n=4796; delta_mrr=-0.0179; p_mrr=0.031; delta_em=-0.0062; p_em=0.118; CI_mrr=[-0.032,-0.004]; notes=high within-session variance on certain prompt templates. Link: https://console.redwood/testing/runs/2026-02-12/1812345999
nathan: so single metric flags but secondary metric is noisy. our current A/B gate uses hard_autofallback for any critical slice mrr<-0.015 with p<0.05.
tara: that feels too trigger-happy when we also get large infra wins. we should weigh cost/latency vs tiny accuracy loss.
alex: agree. suggestion: composite scoring that factors in latency improvement and relative accuracy loss. e.g., allow mrr delta up to -0.02 if p<0.05 only when latency improvement >10% and cost improvement >15%.
nathan: interesting but mixing QOS and economics in a single gate could be risky. Maybe better to add an "economics-exception" path that requires manual OK from release lead.
tara: or a middle ground: auto-block promote (no hard autofallback) but open a fast-review workflow with a 2h replicate run seeded and stratified. If replicate reproduces delta p<0.05, then block or roll back; otherwise allow promote.
eval-bot: historical note: single-metric A/B mrr triggers with n>4000 had reproducibility 78% (n=200). replicate-run reduces false positives by ~60%.
alex: config proposal (example):
```
"ab_gates": [
  {"slice":"code-qa","metric":"mrr","threshold":-0.015,"pvalue":0.05},
  {"slice":"code-qa","metric":"exact_match","threshold":-0.01,"pvalue":0.1}
],
"ab_policy": {
  "hard_autofallback": false,
  "on_single_metric_failure": "replicate_then_manual",
  "replicate_run": {"duration_hours":2,"seed_lock":true,"min_unique_prompts":1200}
}
```
tara: also let's de-duplicate prompts across sessions. we identified a cluster of 180 prompts that repeated across users and inflated n. bump min_unique_prompts to 1200 like above.
nathan: I can patch rollout-config to wire in replicate_then_manual and hook release-bot to page leads if replicate confirms.
release-bot: @oncall-release will be paged when replicate_run -> confirmed regression. runid=2026-02-12-1812345999-01
alex: action items: 1) nathan patches gate cfg + add economics-exception note; 2) tara schedules replicate run (same seed); 3) tara & alex to review replicate outputs in 2h; 4) add one-line doc to runbook describing threshold tradeoffs.
tara: adding small doc blurb: "For A/Bs with >=10% latency or >=15% cost wins, single-metric MRR degradations between -0.015 and -0.03 require replicate-run + manual approve. Hard autofallback only for delta<-0.03 or if replicate confirms."
nathan: quick question: should replicate-run use darker traffic or offline replay?
tara: prefer seeded offline replay to avoid user impact. release-bot supports converting canary sample -> offline replay.
alex: I'm OK with this plan. we preserve safety and buy back faster iteration.
tara: I'll open PR for the config patch and link run. scheduling replicate for 16:10 UTC.
release-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/rollout-config/pull/412 ; diff includes ab_policy change.
